bib.title: Taming the Monster: A Fast and Simple Algorithm for Contextual Bandits

question: Can a contextual bandit algorithm over a general policy class reach the statistically optimal regret while calling a cost-sensitive classification (argmax) oracle only sublinearly often in T?
hypothesis: A coordinate-descent solver for the Randomized UCB convex program, run on an epoch schedule with warm start, keeps optimal regret while cutting oracle calls to about sqrt(KT/ln(|Pi|/delta)); an online variant should be fast and accurate in practice.
contributions: ILOVETOCONBANDITS: epoch-based variant of Randomized UCB with optimal regret O(sqrt(KT ln(T|Pi|/delta)) + K ln(T|Pi|/delta)) (Theorem 2)
Coordinate descent procedure that outputs a sparse distribution over policies, one oracle call per iteration (Theorem 3, Lemma 1)
Epoch schedules (doubling, and warm start with tau_m = m^2) giving ~O(sqrt(KT/ln(|Pi|/delta))) total oracle calls (Lemmas 2, 3)
Lower bound showing the support size, hence oracle calls, cannot be substantially smaller (Theorem 4)
Online Cover variant in Vowpal Wabbit with a proof-of-concept experiment on RCV1

method.summary: Algorithm 1 samples actions from a smoothed distribution over policies and, at epoch boundaries, solves an optimisation problem (OP) with a regret constraint (exploitation) and a per-policy inverse-propensity variance constraint (exploration) by coordinate descent, each iteration costing one argmax-oracle call on a reweighted cost-sensitive dataset. The experiment uses Online Cover, which keeps n online cost-sensitive policies and updates all with doubly robust cost-sensitive examples, on RCV1 converted from supervised to contextual bandit.
method.task: i.i.d. contextual bandit learning; experiment is CCAT document classification from bandit feedback

datasets.name: RCV1 (CCAT document classification)
datasets.split: single online pass; progressive validation on 0/1 loss, no train/test split
datasets.source: Lewis et al. 2004; supervised-to-contextual-bandit transformation of Dudik et al. 2011b (class labels as actions, one minus 0/1-loss as reward)
datasets.preprocessing: TF-IDF features; linear representations; LinUCB run after random projection to 1000 dimensions

models.name: ILOVETOCONBANDITS (Algorithm 1, theory)
models.architecture: distribution Q over a policy class Pi accessed only via an argmax oracle (AMO); psi = 100; mu_m = min{1/2K, sqrt(ln(16 tau_m^2 |Pi|/delta)/(K tau_m))}
models.init_from: Q_0 = 0; warm start uses Q_init = Q_{m-1}

models.name: Online Cover (Algorithm 5)
models.architecture: n online cost-sensitive oracles, each a reduction to squared-loss regression (Algorithms 4 and 5 of Beygelzimer and Langford 2009); uniform distribution over the n policies; doubly robust estimator with an online-trained linear reward function

models.name: Bagging
models.architecture: multiple predictors trained on bootstrap samples give a distribution over actions

models.name: LinUCB
models.architecture: linear UCB (Auer 2002; Chu et al. 2011), 1000-dim random projection

models.name: Supervised one-against-all
models.architecture: one-against-all reduction to binary classification, full-information

training.objective: Theory: solve (OP) over Q in simplex-or-less on policies: sum Q(pi) b_pi <= 2K and for all pi, E_hat[1/Q^mu(pi(x)|x)] <= 2K + b_pi, with b_pi = RegHat_t(pi)/(psi mu). Experiment: online cost-sensitive regression updates with IPS/doubly robust costs.
training.optimizer: Coordinate descent on a potential function (Algorithm 2); online oracle is squared-loss regression reduction
training.regularisation: smoothed projection Q^mu(a|x) = (1-K mu) sum_{pi(x)=a} Q(pi) + mu keeps every action probability at least mu
training.wall_clock: Table 1 seconds: epsilon-greedy 17, Explore-first 2.6, Bagging 275, LinUCB 212 x 10^3, Online Cover 12, Supervised 5.3

other.implementation: Vowpal Wabbit, cbify.cc with --cover; all baselines except LinUCB are modifications of Vowpal Wabbit; default parameters elsewhere

metrics.name: Progressive validation loss
metrics.definition: online 0/1 loss, each example scored before the learner updates on it (Blum et al. 1999)

metrics.name: Regret
metrics.definition: sum_t (r_t(pi*(x_t)) - r_t(a_t)) against the best policy in Pi

metrics.name: Oracle calls / running time
metrics.definition: number of AMO calls over T rounds; seconds in experiment

eval.protocol: Single dataset, best hyperparameter per algorithm reported (searched values in Table 1); no seeds, repeats or confidence intervals stated.

availability.code: Online Cover in Vowpal Wabbit (http://hunch.net/~vw, file cbify.cc, flag --cover)

results.claim: Theorem 2: with probability at least 1-delta the regret of Algorithm 1 after T rounds is O(sqrt(KT ln(T|Pi|/delta)) + K ln(T|Pi|/delta)), the optimal rate up to logs.
results.setup: i.i.d. contextual bandit, finite policy class Pi, K actions, rewards in [0,1], assuming (OP) is solvable each epoch
results.note: theoretical result; proved in Appendices B, C

results.claim: Coordinate descent solves (OP) in a bounded number of iterations, each one oracle call.
results.setup: Q_init = 0; bound 4 ln(1/(K mu_m))/mu_m, which is O~(sqrt(Kt/ln(|Pi|/delta))) in round t

results.claim: With the warm-start epoch schedule the total number of oracle calls over T rounds is sublinear in T, spread over O(sqrt(T)) solves.
results.setup: epoch schedule (3,5) then tau_m = m^2; high probability; bound O~(sqrt(KT/ln(|Pi|/delta)))
results.note: Randomized UCB needs O~(T^5) calls over all T rounds per the paper; this algorithm's net running time is O~(T^1.5 sqrt(K log|Pi|)). Theoretical (Lemma 3).

results.claim: Lower bound: on some instance every distribution satisfying the variance constraint has support at least Omega(sqrt(K tau_M / ln(|Pi| tau_M/delta))), so the oracle-call bounds cannot be improved by sparser distributions.
results.setup: constructed instance with N contexts and (K-1)N zero-regret policies

results.claim: Online Cover reaches progressive validation loss 0.053 on RCV1 contextual-bandit, best among the bandit algorithms and near the 0.051 supervised bound.
results.setup: RCV1 CCAT, 47152 TF-IDF features, linear representation, best hyperparameters; best at cover size n=1
results.quote: Finally, our algorithm achieves the best loss of 0.0530.
results.note: Table 1 prints 0.053 for the same cell.

results.claim: LinUCB with 1000-dimension random projection scores 0.128 progressive validation loss on RCV1.
results.setup: RCV1 CCAT; best setting 10^3 dim, minibatch-10
results.table: Table 1, row P.V. Loss, column LinUCB

results.claim: LinUCB took about 212 x 10^3 seconds (59 hours) versus 12 seconds for Online Cover on RCV1.
results.setup: RCV1 CCAT, LinUCB after random projection to 1000 dims, Intel MKL linear algebra
results.note: Table 1 prints 212 x 10^3 seconds (about 58.9 hours) for LinUCB and 12 for Online Cover.

results.claim: A diagonal-covariance approximation of LinUCB runs in about 1 hour but is worse, error 0.137.
results.setup: RCV1 CCAT, diagonal approximation to the covariance

results.claim: Other baselines on RCV1: epsilon-greedy 0.148, Explore-first 0.081, Bagging 0.059; supervised 0.051.
results.setup: RCV1 CCAT; epsilon=0.1 (epsilon-greedy); 2 x 10^5 exploration examples (Explore-first); 16 bags (Bagging)
results.table: Table 1, row P.V. Loss, columns epsilon-greedy 0.148, Explore-first 0.081, Bagging 0.059, Supervised 0.051
results.note: value shown is epsilon-greedy only; other cells in the table reference

results.claim: Online Cover is under 2.3 times slower than the supervised learner that sees full labels.
results.setup: RCV1; Table 1 times 12 s vs 5.3 s
results.quote: Our algorithm is less than 2.3 times slower and nearly achieves the bound.

limits: The analysis covers the importance-weighted algorithm; the experiment uses Online Cover with a doubly robust estimator, and the authors say analysing Online Cover directly is future work.
Only one dataset (RCV1, supervised-to-bandit conversion) and no repeats, seeds or error bars; authors cite a lack of public contextual bandit datasets.
Best cover size on RCV1 is n=1, so the experiment barely exercises the cover; the authors note the small decaying uniform sampling may itself be adequate exploration.
Computational cost excluding the oracle is still O~((KT)^1.5), above the O(1) per-example update of online supervised learning.
Regret guarantees need i.i.d. contexts and rewards, a finite policy class (VC extension said to be simple), and rewards in [0,1].
LinUCB was run only after random projection to 1000 dimensions; the full-dimensional version is impractical.
Best hyperparameters per algorithm were searched on the same data they are reported on.

terms.definition: given context and reward vector pairs (x_1,r_1)...(x_t,r_t), returns argmax over pi in Pi of the sum of r_tau(pi(x_tau)); a cost-sensitive classification learner
unbiased estimate R_hat_t(pi) = (1/t) sum_i r_i(a_i) 1{pi(x_i)=a_i} / p_i(a_i)
Q^mu(a|x) = (1 - K mu) sum_{pi: pi(x)=a} Q(pi) + mu, so every action has probability at least mu
sum over t of r_t(pi*(x_t)) - r_t(a_t), relative to the best policy pi* in Pi
online evaluation where each example is scored before the learner updates on it (Blum et al. 1999)
